result.note: Tests the two-thirds threshold under the anti-defection law and the Speaker's role in disqualification petitions; personalities skipped.

questions.prompt: In June 2026, six of the nine Lok Sabha MPs of the Shiv Sena (UBT) joined the faction led by Eknath Shinde. Consider the following statements:
items: Six of nine MPs meets the two-thirds threshold that shields the group from disqualification under India's anti-defection law.
The Thackeray camp signalled it would approach the Supreme Court directly, bypassing the Lok Sabha Speaker.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 2 is wrong: the Thackeray camp said it would first seek disqualification before the Lok Sabha Speaker, and only failing that go to the Supreme Court. The anti-defection law otherwise unseats lawmakers who switch parties, which is why the number six mattered.
questions.source: six of nine is the two-thirds threshold that shields the group from disqualification under India's anti-defection law, which otherwise unseats lawmakers who switch parties.
